thread:
Priya: Heads up — noticed steady KV cache growth on host gpu-12 where tenant 'bluefox' runs lots of longctx requests. Memory climbs after ~5k tok conversations, not evicting as expected. p99 mem delta +18% over 6h. Suspect reuse signature mismatch causing low page reclaim.

Ethan: do you have pprof/heap or kv-residency logs? post links pls.

Priya: link -> http://graf.redwood/internal/dashboards/kv-residency?host=gpu-12 ; quick snippets pasted: 
```
kv_resident_pages{tenant="bluefox"} 1.32e6
kv_evictions_total{tenant="bluefox"} 120
kv_page_reuse_hits{tenant="bluefox"} 3
```
also seeing slab_frag_ratio ~0.62 which feels high.

Nikhil: hmm reuse_hits super low. Could be longctx prefixes pinned by prefix-hash change. Remember we rolled kernel selection tweak last week that reduced eager pagewalks. Might be side-effect.

Ana: can we try a quick config tweak in staging: `tenant_cache_sample_rate=0.05` and `lease_timeout=20s`? want to see if forcing more sampling increases evict signals.

Priya: kicking off a staging canary now. config snippet: 
```
routes:
  - tenant: bluefox
    kv:
      sample_rate: 0.05
      lease_timeout_ms: 20000
```

SRE-bot: ALERT: KV page growth > 15% for 1h on gpu-12 (incident id: inc-2026-07-11-73)

Ethan: also double-check batching heuristics — if batch sizes climb with those longctx requests, the KV prefix cache lifetime can increase. Interaction between kernel selection (fewer pagewalks) + larger batches may be keeping pages hot.

Nikhil: quick experiment idea — enable lane compaction every 1000 ops and flip on pagewalk defrag. I can push a small runtime patch: `runtime/kv: compaction_threshold=1000` and `pagewalk_defrag=true`.

Priya: staging results after ~30m: evictions up ~2x (which is good), resident pages down -9%, tail latency p50 +2ms (within SLO). Observed slab_frag_ratio improved to ~0.48.

Ana: prod rollout proposal: staggered enabling across hosts: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with canary checks (evict rate, resident pages, p50/p95 latency, qos_loss). Auto-rollback if qos_loss > 0.5% in any window.

Ethan: also add automated audit: compute noisy-neighbor score per tenant (based on sustained resident growth, reuse_hits, and request churn). If score > 0.7 then apply soft throttle to KV residency by lowering sample_rate.

Priya: will open follow-up thread with perf traces, pprof heap dump, and the exact runtime patch diff. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Nikhil: LGTM

Ana: adding runbook checklist to the canary PR: monitor links, roll windows, rollback steps, owners.

Priya: assigned follow-ups: (1) PR for compaction/defrag (Nikhil) (2) canary config + dashboard (Ana) (3) heap dump + traces (Priya) (4) noisy-neighbor audit metric (Ethan).
